headline: High: shared workspace and overlapping data flows create prompt-injection, leakage, and cascading-error risks; compliance risk is moderate.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Notion AI can read workspace pages and databases, and the profile says shared workspace state exists across instances. Rasa can ingest messages from chat channels, so a malicious Notion page or copied content could be forwarded into the bot flow. The interaction is inferred, not directly documented, so uncertainty keeps this at medium rather than low.
conditions: IF content from Notion pages is copied into a Rasa channel or webhook payload
IF Rasa treats user-supplied text as instructions or routing data without provenance checks
mitigations: Add a provenance banner to all Notion-to-bot handoffs
Strip markup and instruction-like text before forwarding
Require a human review step for any copied workspace content
Use separate workspaces or channels for bot prompts
requires-engineering: add provenance-aware filtering between the agents

B_data_leakage.rationale: Notion AI touches workspace pages and team knowledge base content, while Rasa handles text/voice and can connect to external messaging APIs. Because Notion shares workspace state across instances, sensitive workspace content could be exposed if it is forwarded into Rasa outputs or logs. The pairwise leakage path is plausible but not directly evidenced, so medium fits best.
conditions: IF workspace pages contain sensitive internal content
IF Rasa connectors log or relay message text to external channels
mitigations: Limit which pages can be copied into bot workflows
Disable verbose logging on Rasa connectors
Redact secrets before forwarding text
Review outbound channel settings for message retention
requires-engineering: implement DLP checks on shared content

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Notion AI has no filesystem write, shell, or git modification, while Rasa only shows allowlisted network egress and no explicit write surface. That makes direct write-write conflict unlikely. The only plausible conflict is shared mutable workspace state on the Notion side, so the blast radius is limited and low is appropriate.
conditions: IF both agents are wired to the same mutable workspace or ticket queue
IF Rasa is extended with a write-back integration not shown in the profile
mitigations: Keep the agents on separate mutable resources
Avoid concurrent edits to the same workspace object
Serialize any write-back steps through one operator
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources

D_cascading_error.rationale: Notion AI produces grounded workspace answers, and Rasa is a dialogue system that can act on text it receives from channels. If Rasa treats Notion output as authoritative, an incorrect summary can cascade into wrong replies or actions. Because no verification layer is documented, the interaction is plausible in default integrations and merits medium severity.
conditions: IF Notion output is pasted or piped into Rasa without validation
IF Rasa uses that text as the source of truth for customer responses
mitigations: Require citation checks before Rasa uses Notion text
Add a confidence threshold for auto-replies
Route uncertain answers to a human agent
Log source documents alongside generated replies
requires-engineering: build a verification step between agents

E_compliance.rationale: Notion AI processes workspace pages and team knowledge base content, while Rasa handles text/voice and can send data through third-party messaging APIs. The profiles do not show matching retention or residency controls, so a mismatch in handling the same data class is plausible. Because the compliance posture is undocumented rather than clearly conflicting, medium is the safest choice.
conditions: IF regulated or personal data is present in Notion workspace content
IF Rasa connectors retain or transmit that data outside the intended jurisdiction
mitigations: Classify data before sending it to either agent
Restrict regulated data to a separate workspace
Check connector retention settings
Document a DPA and residency review
requires-engineering: align retention and residency policies
